content.title: Official Blind Review #1
content.review_assessment:_thoroughness_in_paper: I read the paper at least twice and used my best judgement in assessing the paper.
content.review:
Summary: this paper introduces 2 new entropy-based metrics that can be used to explain what happens in hidden layers of image neural nets. These metrics are information discarding (how much original info from the features is flowing through a particular layer) and reconstruction uncertainty (how much can be  recovered to the original input)
Overall, it is an interesting idea and it looks less ad-hoc than other methods (gradient based, inversion based etc).  The  initial ideas and approximations are well explained, but applying it all to neural nets is not that clear- I did find it hard understanding how it all works together, and an algorithm for computing all the metrics would in a table would be much easier to follow.  I also find it hard to draw any conclusions from observing the values of the metrics (please see below) on different architectures (see comment #4).

Detailed questions/comments
1) How is delta_f computed? Is it a variance of activations values over the batch? Or something else
2) How is concept defined? It seems that the paper goes under the assumption that there is a magic subset f  (in a hidden layer), but where is it coming from. For a trained nn, how do you define what this f is?
3) How does the proposed method apply to non image settings, for example a simple binary classification with dense features. What are the concept features, where is the ground truth segment etc
4) Figure 3: what conclusions do we draw from it? Which modification of res net was giving better performance? Should we look for networks with higher SID, harmonic mean of SID and reconstruction or something else How do you practically use the metrics you propose to chose the best architecture. The only thing you say is that deep DNN has higher SID and RU. Struggling to understand what use this is. 
From the appendix, Section A is actually more interesting and illustrative than what you put into experiments in the main paper. 
5) Experiments didn't really compare your proposed method with any of alternative methods. A couple of illustrative pictures with what your method shows and gradient based shows for example would go a long way
6) How do you train a reconstruction network to ensure minimum required efficiency. What is the architecture you chose for it?
7) If these proposed metrics are correlated with generalization (which is not clear yet), do you  think it can be introduces as a new regularization during training.

Minor: 
- I really would suggest to have separate captions for each figure, instead of one long caption and top left, top right etc. It is really hard to parse
- In appendix instead of such a large dump of pics, chose a couple that really illustrate that you are trying to show, and add the explanations from alternative methods (gradient based for example) to demonstrate the benefits of your method

content.title: Responses
content.comment:
We thank all reviewers for their constructive comments. We will try our best to answer all your questions.

Q1: Ask for the computation of delta_f.

A: Thank you. We have already answered this question behind the Equation (5). Please see Sec.3.1 for a detailed introduction of \delta_f. “\delta_f^2 is computed by averaging over all images to normalize the activation magnitude.” Nevertheless, we will further clarify the computation of \delta_f in the final paper.


Q2: Ask for the definition of the subset f.

A: In the paragraph “Both SID and RU are derived ……” in Section 3, we use f=h(x) to denote an intermediate-layer feature of the DNN. F_c is a small range of features with the center of f. In this paper, there is no explicit definition for F_c, but there exists a latent space.


Q3: In Figure 3, “what conclusions do we draw from it? ……”

A: A good question. We have discussed the conclusion of Figure 3 in the paragraph “Comparison between different DNNs for various tasks ……” and “Concentration of information discarding: ……” in Section 4. Subfigure (a), (b) show that a deep DNN usually has higher SID and RU. Subfigure (c) shows that high layers are more concentrated on the foreground than low layers. 


Q4: About the comparison of our methods and alternative methods.

A: Thank you. We have compared the visualization of our metrics with previous methods such as CAM, Grad_CAM in Figure 1. It shows that traditional pixel-wise saliency has issues in generality and coherency. Our metrics can provide consistent measures of information discarding that enable faithful comparisons over layers and networks. We will re-organize the figures to provide more detailed comparisons in the final paper.


Q5: Ask for the architecture of the reconstruction network.

A: Thank you. We have introduced that we trained auto-encoders for image reconstruction in paragraph “Comparisons between different DNNs for various tasks: ……”, Sec. 4. We revised the architecture of ResNet-20, ResNet-32, ResNet-44 for auto-encoders and decoders in our experiments.


Q6: Suggestions about the separate captions for each figure.

A: Thanks for your suggestions. We will re-organize our figures in the paper.

content.title: Official Blind Review #3
content.review_assessment:_checking_correctness_: I assessed the sensibility of the derivations and theory.
content.review:
This paper proposes two measures of information discarding during forward propagation of a neural network. The paper presents how to calculate the two measures, compare them with alternatives, and demonstrate their values in different networks and different tasks. 

The paper is in general well written. However, first, the proposed measures do not seem to be well motivated--what is the essential purpose of having the measures? Second, although the intuition is clear, the proposed methods do not seem be well justified. As the authors pointed out, the proposed measures are related to the mutual information I(F;X), where F is the considered inner representation. Why are the proposed measures superior to alternatives? Why are they better than the information bottleneck one (in the extreme case, to make it task-independent, one may drop the term involving Y)? Furthermore, on the technical side, the raw input as well as the reconstructed input is highly non-iid (independent and identically distributed), so is it sensible to calculate the total entropy H(X_c) as the sum of the individual ones for the pixels (in equation 2, for example) at all? Third, the authors tried to justify that the proposed measures are consistent and faithful in Section 4, but I failed to see if from the panels in Figure 1. What is the exact definition of coherency here?

content.title: Responses
content.comment:
We thank all reviewers for their constructive comments. We will try our best to answer all your questions.

Q1: About the motivation of our proposed metrics.

A: Thank you. We have introduced our motivation in the second paragraph of Section 1. In this paper, we aim to propose generic and coherent metrics to diagnose the representation capacity of DNNs. These metrics could be used for comprehensive and fair comparisons over different layers and different DNNs. We will further clarify our motivation in the final paper.


Q2: “Why are the proposed measures superior to alternatives? Why are they better than the information bottleneck one?”

A: A good question. We have compared our methods with the information bottleneck theory in Section 3.3. First, our metrics have much stronger connections to existing mathematical theories than other explanation methods. Thus, our metrics can provide a fine-grained analysis of information discarding. Second, the information bottleneck principle analyzes DNNs on the sample level, and it is hard to compute. We analyze DNNs on the pixel level, and our metrics are easier to compute.


Q3: “the raw input as well as the …… as the sum of the individual ones for the pixels at all?”

A: A good question. In the paragraph “The core challenge ……”, Sec. 3.1 and the paragraph “The above entropy ……”, Section 3.2, we have assumed that x’ follows a Gaussian distribution. Although the fact is that pixels of the input image are dependent, we can use this assumption to formulate the problem. We will further clarify this issue in the final paper.


Q4: Ask for the definition of coherency.

A: Thanks for your comment. We have answered your question in the paragraph “Coherency: As generic metrics, ……”, Sec. 1. Coherency ensures that our metrics are agnostic to the network architecture and the task. Thus, we can fairly compare different DNNs and different layers with our metrics. As shown in Figure 1 (left, bottom), the value of SID and RU increased with the layer number, which showed the process of information discarding in the DNN.

content.title: Official Blind Review #2
content.review_assessment:_checking_correctness_: I did not assess the derivations or theory.
content.review:
The paper aims to understand and interpret feature representation in DNNS by proposing two entropy-based at pixel-level metrics called Strict information discard (SID) and reconstruction uncertainty (RU). The new metrics are used to diagnosis the generality and coherency of DNN models. 
Overall, quantifying and interpret feature representation learning in DNNS are important and interesting topics. Two proposed metrics have clear intuitions. However, the paper needs to be improved to be published at the top-notch venues. 
Section 3 contains the main contributions, however, there are many aspects which is not rigorously defined. Hence, it is difficult to justify the soundness of the metrics. Some unclear details are as follows
1/ What is X_c, is it the empirical distribution of data or data distribution in general or what else? 
2/ In Eq(6), to compute the concentration, do we need the ground truth?
3/ The proposed metrics are mentioned to be related to the information-bottleneck principle but the paper does not describe it in detail. How are they similar and different? Can newly proposed metrics replace the information-bottleneck principle? 
4/The paper mentioned that the perturbation-based methods are heuristic-based, why are the entropy-based methods not heuristic? Is there any theoretical guarantee that they reflect the idea of SID and RU?
Moreover, the experiments only demonstrate how SID and RU works in several datasets and settings. There is no comparison with other works in the literature, e.g. the information-bottleneck principle.

content.title: Responses
content.comment:
We thank all reviewers for their constructive comments. We will try our best to answer all your questions.

Q1: “What is X_c, is it the empirical distribution of data or data distribution in general or what else?”

A: Thank you. We have introduced X_c and F_c in Section 3. In this paper, there is no explicit representation for X_c, and it is a latent space for x’ that represents a specific object.


Q2: About the ground-truth to compute the concentration.

A: Yes, we need the ground truth. We have already answered your concern in the paragraph “Concentration of information discarding ……”. We use \Lambda to denote the ground truth segment of the target object in x.


Q3: About the relationship with the information bottleneck principle. “How are they similar and different?”

A: A good question. We have discussed the relationship with the information bottleneck principle in Section 3.3. The conditional entropy of SID and that of RU are related to the mutual information if we limit our attention to a local range of features. As for the difference, the information bottleneck principle analyzes DNNs at the sample level. Our research is able to provide a fine-grained analysis of pixel-wise information discarding. In addition, our metrics are easier to compute. We will further clarify the relationship in the final paper.


Q4: “Why are the entropy-based …… SID and RU?”

A: Thank you. As the answer to Q3, the conditional entropy of SID and RU are related to the mutual information. Thus, our metrics have stronger connections to existing mathematical theories than other explanation methods, including perturbation-based methods.


Q5: About the comparison with other works in the literature.

A: Thank you. We have already compared our metrics with other works such as CAM and Grad_CAM in Figure 1. It showed that traditional pixel-wise saliency has issues in generality and coherency. Our metrics can provide consistent measures of information discarding that enable faithful comparisons over layers and networks.
